$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

OPEN REQUESTS DO NOT SURVIVE: a relaunch cannot answer a pre-shutdown permission or question (probe c: the old request is not re-emitted). These must be closed on load as an explicit expired state, which needs a new field or kind, not the bare resolved badge.

CONCURRENT WRITE: saving from on_output or send_through without a revision or order lock can let an older snapshot overwrite a newer one. Use the publish pattern (mod.rs:132-140), write atomically (temp file, then rename), and never hold Inner across disk I/O.

plan.intent: Session/inbox model for D2, Rust and TS and UI together in one commit. (a) New SessionStatus::Suspended (wire: suspended): not running but resumable because it holds a valid claude_session_id. (b) InboxItem gains expired: bool (expired implies resolved=true; resolved stays monotonic so the state.ts merge rules still hold) and result_text: Option<String> (full result text on Result items, Finished and Error, capped at MAX_RESULT_BYTES=262144 on a char boundary; summary stays 300 chars). (c) SessionState::suspend(now): drains pending, marks every open Permission/Question item resolved+expired, sets Suspended if claude_session_id is Some, else Ended; pushes no Error item. (d) A CanUseTool whose request_id is already in pending is ignored (no second item). (e) claude_session_id is accepted from Init only if it is a canonical 8-4-4-4-12 hex UUID (hand-rolled check, no new crate), else ignored. (f) Serialize+Deserialize on SessionStatus, InboxKind, InboxItem, Question, QuestionOption, plus a serde-able PersistedSession (status, last_activity_at, last_message, claude_session_id, inbox, next_item, unknown_count) with to/from conversions; Pending is NOT persisted. (g) TS: types.ts adds suspended, expired, result_text; ipc.ts decoders validate them (missing or mistyped expired throws, as today); InboxItemView renders an Expired badge and a distinct .card.expired style, never Resolved, and shows result_text in a scrollable pre-wrap block on finished/error items; SessionList LABELS/LIVE get suspended (label Paused, not live); App.css rules for both.

plan.intent: Persistence under app_data_dir plus a clean shutdown path. New session/store.rs: Snapshot { schema: 1, revision, next_session, next_project, projects: [{id, name, path}], sessions: [{id, project_id, project_name, started_at, state: PersistedSession}] } at app_data_dir/state.json. save = serialize, write state.json.tmp, sync_all, std::fs::rename over state.json (atomic replace on Windows). load = Ok(None) if absent, Ok(snapshot) if schema == 1, Err(UnknownSchema{found}) or Err(Unreadable) otherwise; on Err the file is never touched and saving is DISABLED for the run. Writer: one background thread fed by a channel. Sessions computes the snapshot under Inner with revision += 1, takes emit_order, drops Inner, then sends (revision, snapshot) - the publish() shape at mod.rs:132-140. The writer coalesces to the newest and skips any revision <= last written, so an older snapshot never overwrites a newer one; Inner is never held across disk I/O. Saves fire from publish() and add_project(). Restore: Sessions::restore(snapshot) rebuilds projects (path re-validated with is_dir; a missing folder stays in the store but is hidden from list_projects and unusable by start/resume; ids come from a persisted next_project counter instead of the vec index) and sessions (every non-Ended/Failed session goes through SessionState::suspend, which also expires items a crash left open). next_session, next_project and per-session next_item are persisted, so sN/pN/item ids never collide. Shutdown, the PLAN-KILLER fix: Sessions::shutdown() replaces kill_all on RunEvent::Exit. Under Inner it sets shutting_down = true and suspends every live session, computes the final snapshot, drops Inner, flushes it synchronously (waits for the writer), THEN kills children. on_output returns early with no state change, no publish and no save once shutting_down is set, so the reader Exit(1) after the job kill can never become Failed + an error item. Loud failure: a storage_status IPC command returns {ok: true} or {ok: false, reason: unknown_schema_version | unreadable, found_version?} with no path in it; App.tsx shows a persistent banner that history was not loaded and will not be saved this run. Absolute project paths live only in this Rust-written file and never cross IPC.

architect.rationale: Single-loop: one builder, one branch in the orchestra git repo, slices built in order. Not a diamond because the D2 pieces share seams: state.rs is edited by s1, s2 and s3; mod.rs by s2 and s3; lib.rs by s2 (load + shutdown) and s4 (plugin); ipc.ts, ipc.test.ts and App.css by s1 and s2; InboxItemView.tsx by s1 and s3. Only s4 and s5 are content-disjoint, and s4 still shares lib.rs; fewer than 3 disjoint slices, so fanning out would only manufacture merge conflicts. Risk tags: s1 high - changes the IPC schema on both sides, a wrong decoder silently drops whole payloads (ipc.ts:133-155), and it shares state.rs with s2/s3. s2 high - writes absolute user paths to disk, has ordering logic a unit test only partly sees (revision ordering, no Inner across I/O), owns the PLAN-KILLER shutdown fix, and shares mod.rs/state.rs/lib.rs. s3 high - spawns a child with an argument derived from persisted data (flag injection if the UUID check is wrong) and shares mod.rs/state.rs. s4 high - shares lib.rs with s2 and adds a native dependency (Cargo.lock); the visible-display guarantee is only partly testable. s5 low - prose in two files no other slice touches, verifiable by grep. Scout risks resolved: PLAN-KILLER -> s2 shutdown() with a shutting_down flag, suspend before kill, synchronous final save, on_output ignored afterwards; test quit_records_suspended_not_failed. Open requests -> expired flag (s1) in Rust+TS+UI, rendered Expired, never Resolved. ID counters -> persisted (s2). Concurrent saves -> revision + ordered handoff + coalescing writer + temp/rename (s2). Absolute paths -> only in the Rust-written store, never over IPC, is_dir on load, exception documented (s2, s5). Resume -> lazy (s3) with Ended fallback. Duplicate control_request -> deduped by request_id (s1). Done item -> Finished extended with result_text (s1). Window-state -> no capability, our own visible-display check (s4). Note: a stale D1 script in the shared scratchpad briefly overwrote this key with the D1 diamond plan during this architect run; this write replaces it in full.

resume_policy.recommended: lazy - restored sessions are Suspended (shown Paused) and respawn with --resume only when the user replies; zero processes and zero tokens at launch
resume_policy.alternative: auto-resume on launch - every unfinished session respawns at startup; costs tokens and N processes per launch, and a resumed claude does nothing until it gets a user line anyway (probe a)

unknown_schema_behaviour.recommended: start with empty in-memory state, leave state.json untouched, disable saving for the run, show a persistent banner via storage_status
alternatives: show a native error dialog and quit
rename the file aside (state.json.unreadable-<ts>) and start fresh

done_item.alternative: new InboxKind done - duplicates Finished and needs a decoder change for no behaviour gain

suspended_status.alternative: reuse Idle for restored sessions - hides that no process is running and conflates a turn interrupted mid-work with a finished one

absolute_paths.recommended: store absolute project paths in app_data_dir/state.json (Rust-only), re-validate on load, record the exception in orchestra/CLAUDE.md
absolute_paths.alternative: do not persist projects; restored sessions become Ended and the user re-picks folders - loses resume entirely

window_state_capability.recommended: grant nothing; the plugin is used from Rust only
window_state_capability.alternative: grant window-state:default - only needed if the frontend ever calls the plugin, which D2 does not

not_doing: Auto-resume at launch (lazy resume recommended; alternative at the gate)
Retention, pruning or a size cap on persisted inbox history; a clear-history action
Persisting the transcript stream, cost or usage (D3)
Re-emitting or re-answering requests that were open at quit - they expire

s1.summary: PASS. Re-ran on tip 4c6bf40: cargo test 67 passed/0 failed with all six named s1 tests ok (their bodies are unchanged since e85873c); npm test 25/25 incl. the four new decodeInboxItem cases and 'accepts suspended'; npm run build (tsc && vite build) exit 0. Re-derived from the diff: Rust serde names (suspended, expired, result_text, snake_case) match types.ts/ipc.ts, and expired/result_text are always serialized so no payload is dropped; is_uuid checks 36 bytes with hyphens only at 8/13/18/23 and hex elsewhere, so a leading '-' is impossible; truncate_bytes walks back to a char boundary (no panic on 2-byte chars, tested); suspend drains pending, sets resolved+expired only on open Permission/Question, picks Suspended/Ended on claude_session_id, pushes no item; dedupe checks pending by request_id; Expired badge is exclusive of Resolved; LABELS/LIVE carry suspended. Diff is exactly the 8 approved files; author njcurtis3, no trailer. Notes: is_uuid accepts uppercase hex; suspended is not is_over (later slices handle the exit seam); mergeInbox keeps the old copy's expired.

findings.issue: is_uuid uses is_ascii_hexdigit, so uppercase UUIDs ('0B9F6A2C-...') are accepted. Not an injection risk (length, hyphen positions and first byte are all pinned, no leading '-'), but 'canonical' in the intent arguably means lowercase. Claude emits lowercase, so no observed failure.

is_over() is still Ended|Failed only, so a Suspended session still accepts apply()/mark_exit(): within s1 alone, suspend() followed by mark_exit(Some(1)) would go Failed with an error item. No caller of suspend exists in s1; at tip, shutdown() sets shutting_down so readers are ignored, and lazy resume needs Suspended to stay non-terminal. Flagged for the s2/s3 reviewers, not a blocker here.

mergeInbox (not in s1's file list) keeps `have`'s fields and ORs only resolved, so if an event copy with expired:false arrived before an inbox-loaded snapshot with expired:true, the merged item would show Resolved rather than Expired. Unreachable today because expiry happens only at restore (before the UI loads) or at shutdown; a one-line `expired: have.expired || i.expired` would make it hold by construction.

from_persisted does not enforce expired => resolved on load; a hand-edited file with expired:true,resolved:false on an Ended/Failed session (where suspend() is a no-op) would render Expired with live Allow/Deny buttons. Only from a corrupted file; normalizing in from_persisted would close it.

s2.summary: PASS. Read 126d194 (8 files, all in the approved list; author njcurtis3, no trailer) and the untouched seams (start/stop/send_through, state.rs suspend/is_over, job-object kill). Re-ran cargo test on tip 4c6bf40 (67 passed, 0 failed, all 8 named s2 tests present and passing), npm test (25 passed), npm run build (built). Re-derived the quit fix: shutdown sets shutting_down and suspends under Inner, next_snapshot returns None once shutting_down so no later publish can queue a save, a straggler snapshot computed before shutdown carries a lower revision and is skipped once the final one is written, and kill runs only after flush acks, so the reader Exit(1) is dropped by on_output's early return. Lock order inner -> emit_order holds everywhere; Inner is never held across the channel send or disk. Atomic save, unknown-schema refusal (no writer, file untouched, path-free status, persistent banner) and restore (counters, is_dir, suspend+expire) match the plan. Notes: the snapshot clones the whole unbounded history under Inner on every stdout line; the schema test's 'save attempt' is vacuous; flush has a 5s timeout.

findings.title: Full-history snapshot on every publish, unbounded history
findings.detail: next_snapshot clones every session's inbox (result_text up to 262144 bytes per Finished/Error item) under Inner for every stdout line via on_output->publish, and the writer rewrites + sync_all's the whole file per batch. Coalescing bounds disk writes but not the clone under the lock. With no pruning across runs, a long-lived history (hundreds of finished turns) means tens of MB cloned under Inner per streamed line. Not a correctness failure today; a follow-up should cap/prune history or snapshot only dirty sessions.

findings.title: refuses_unknown_schema_version 'after a save attempt' half is vacuous
findings.detail: The test asserts writer.is_none() twice and re-reads the bytes; nothing attempts a save. The guarantee holds structurally (lib.rs passes open()'s None writer to Sessions::with_writer; next_snapshot/queue_save/shutdown are all gated on self.writer), so it is adequate as a proof of 'no writer exists', but a stronger test would build Sessions with the None writer, add_project/start/shutdown, and then compare bytes.

findings.title: quit test cannot detect kill-before-flush
findings.detail: The fake's kill() only sets a flag and emits no Exit, so reordering kill ahead of the flush in shutdown() would still pass quit_records_suspended_not_failed. Code order is correct today (save+flush then kill).

findings.title: Bounded final flush and swallowed save errors
findings.detail: Writer::flush waits at most 5s; if the final write is slower the process exits and the rename never happens, leaving the previous revision (atomic, never torn). A rename failure (target held open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE, e.g. AV) is swallowed and retried only by a later save, so the final snapshot can be lost silently. Both degrade to the crash path, which restore() handles by suspending and expiring open items. Acceptable; no user-visible signal.

findings.title: Pre-existing: start() racing shutdown spawns an untracked child
findings.detail: start() inserts the session, drops Inner, then spawns; if shutdown runs in between, the new proc is not in shutdown's kill list. Same race existed with kill_all; the job object closes on process exit and kills the tree, and the child's output is ignored once shutting_down, so no state or disk effect.

s3.summary: PASS. Re-ran at tip 4c6bf40: cargo test 67 passed, 0 failed, all six named s3 tests ok; npm test 25 passed; npm run build exit 0. Probed real claude 2.1.296 in a scratch dir outside the repo using the fixed ARGS plus --resume with an all-zero UUID and stdin closed. It returned one result line (error_during_execution, is_error:true, no result field, requested id echoed) and exited 1. So the reconstructed is_error:true is correct, and non-zero exit while resuming is a second, independent path to Ended. Flag injection traced: ClaudeSessionId has a private field and is built only by parse(is_uuid). build_args appends only --resume and that id after the unchanged ARGS. Reply text goes to stdin JSON, never to argv. The gate prevents a double spawn, expired answers are refused before any process is touched, restore spawns nothing, and the Weak self-reference cannot panic or form a cycle. Notes: a folder deleted while the app runs leaves the session Paused with a generic error; a transient API error on the first resumed turn ends the conversation for good; every exit now kills the job.

findings.title: A folder deleted after launch is not caught by the missing-folder path
findings.detail: resume_with relies on Projects::get, whose missing flag is set only by Projects::restore at load time. If the folder is deleted while the app is running, reply on a Suspended session reaches process::spawn with a nonexistent current_dir. cmd.spawn fails, the session goes back to Suspended through abort_resume, and the user gets 'failed to start claude' with no Error item. Every retry repeats this. The test missing_project_folder_ends_without_spawn sets up a rig r, deletes its folder, and then never replies on r; it covers only the restore-time case. A path.is_dir() check before spawning would close this.

findings.title: A transient error on the first resumed turn ends the conversation for good
findings.detail: Any is_error Result before the first successful Result is treated as a failed resume, as the spec says. That includes an API overload, rate limit or auth error on the reply turn of a resume that actually worked. The session goes to Ended (terminal, with no UI path to reply again) and the process is killed, although claude_session_id is still valid. A later slice could check the subtype or num_turns, or the errors text, to tell 'No conversation found' apart from a turn error.

findings.title: on_output now kills the process job on every exit, not only on a failed resume
findings.detail: The 'dead' check runs after every output, including Output::Exit. A normal Exit that marks the session Ended or Failed now calls p.kill(), which is job.terminate on Windows. Before this change the job lived until the ProcessHandle was dropped. Detached grandchildren that do not hold the stdout pipe are now killed when claude exits instead of later. The comment ('A line can end a session only when a resume failed') understates this. The effect is probably fine, but the behaviour changed for every session, not only resumed ones.

findings.title: Fixture's result session_id differs from the requested id; real claude echoes the requested one
findings.detail: resume_unknown_id.jsonl has the error text naming ...0001 and session_id ...0002. The real capture echoes the requested id in session_id, and the README itself says 'the id echoed'. Nothing reads Result.session_id, so behaviour is unaffected. The real capture also has is_error:true, which confirms the reconstructed field, so the README caveat could be replaced with the observed shape.

s4.summary: PASS. Re-ran on tip 4c6bf40: cargo test 67/0 failed incl. the 3 named window:: tests; cargo build exit 0; both greps (0, 2). Re-derived from registry source: plugin 2.5.0 needs tauri ^2.12 (single 2.12.2 in tree); lock delta +16, nothing removed; registered only under cfg(desktop); capabilities untouched, no frontend use. Ordering holds: setup() builds config windows, window_created goes via run_on_main_thread, which runs inline on the main thread, and setup runs in the Ready handler there, so restore precedes ensure_visible. outer_position, outer_size and work_area are all physical; empty monitor list returns early, no panic paths. Notes: outer_size is fed to set_size, which sets the INNER size, so a recentred window ends up a frame larger than the clamp and slightly off-centre; the 50 px strip rule recentres a window whose top is 1 px above the work area. Diff is the 4 approved files; author njcurtis3, no trailer. Human-read monitor test not run.

findings.issue: ensure_visible reads window.outer_size() but applies the clamped result with window.set_size(PhysicalSize), which tauri-runtime-wry maps to set_inner_size. Input: saved 5000x3000 rect whose corner intersects the primary but title bar is off-screen -> after recentre the OUTER window is the 1920x1040 work area plus the frame (~16 x ~40 physical px on Windows), so its bottom edge sits under the taskbar, and centring is off by the same amount. The plugin then saves that larger inner size on exit, so each recentre grows the window by one frame. Title bar stays reachable, so the slice's guarantee holds; fix is to clamp against inner_size (or subtract outer-inner delta) before set_size.

The plan's rule requires the full top min(h,50) px strip inside one work area, so a window at y=-1 (title bar 49 px visible and fully grabbable, e.g. dragged to the top edge with Snap off, or a top-docked taskbar overlapping by a pixel) is judged not visible and recentred on launch. Likewise a strip split 60/60 across two adjacent monitors is rejected because the 100 px must lie in ONE monitor. Matches the plan literally; a smaller height threshold (e.g. 20 px) or union of monitors would avoid false recentres.

The named test rect_on_removed_monitor_is_recentred exercises the pure function only. In the real removed-monitor case the plugin skips set_position when the saved rect intersects no monitor (tauri-plugin-window-state 2.5.0 src/lib.rs:211), the OS places the window, and ensure_visible usually finds it visible and does nothing; the restored size is NOT clamped then (e.g. a 2560x1440 size from a removed 4K monitor on a 1080p primary). Consistent with the intent (clamp only when not visible) but the human-read check is what actually covers this path.

The dependency is unconditional while registration is cfg(desktop); harmless for a desktop-only app, but a mobile target would still compile the crate. Could be moved under [target.'cfg(not(any(target_os = "android", target_os = "ios")))'.dependencies].
